source_text:
5.10
Οτι οὐκ ε στιν ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐ τῶν ἀλήθεια, ἡ
καρδία αὐτῶν ματαία.
Πρότερον, οὐδεμία ἀλήθεια, η ὁ Χριστός· καὶ τάχα τὸ
Τάφος ἀνεῳγμένος ὁ λάρυγξ αὐτῶν.
δεύτερον, ἠνέγκατο αὐτῶν ἐπι βουλήν.
Νεκρῶν ε ργων πεπληρωμένος.
pass_a_gloss: Because not there-is in the mouth of-them truth, the heart of-them vain. First, no-one truth except the Christ; and perhaps the second, it-bore of-them a-plot. Tomb having-been-opened the throat of-them. Of-dead works having-been-filled.
pass_b_english: “Because there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain” (Psalm 5:10). First, there is no truth except Christ; and perhaps the second clause has borne their plot.
“An opened tomb is their throat” (Psalm 5:10). Filled with dead works.

choices.why: After οὐδεμία, ἤ is exceptive: no truth except Christ. Not a second option ‘or the Christ’.
The two members of the lemma (mouth / heart), not ‘previously’.
Aorist middle of φέρω: the vain heart bore their plot. Not ‘caused’.
ἐπιβουλή = plot, as in 5.9 ἐπιβουλεύοντες. Not κατὰ βουλήν ‘according to counsel’.
Genitive of content with πεπληρωμένος (throat filled). Not ‘works of the dead’ as owners.
Lock prints the second lemma between καὶ τάχα τὸ and δεύτερον; two-column OCR. Restore as its own lemma, comment Νεκρῶν ἔργων πεπληρωμένος.
rejected: perhaps the opened tomb of their throat (one sentence)

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
